result_text:
`all_files.zip` now takes its entry names from the configured aspect names. I compiled the `reports` module offline and it builds. I haven't run any tests or exercised the renamed-aspect case.

The change is in `reports/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/reports/dataexporters/DataExporter.java`, in the zip block at the end of the export. The five scope aspects (main, test, generated, build and deployment, other) are now looked up through `DataExportUtils.getAspectFileListFileName(aspect, "")`. That is the same call that writes the loose `aspect_<name>.txt` files, so the read-back name always matches the written one.

- **Default configuration:** the entries stay `aspect_main.txt`, `aspect_test.txt`, `aspect_generated.txt`, `aspect_build_and_deployment.txt` and `aspect_other.txt`, in that order.
- **Renamed aspect:** with `buildAndDeployment`, the fourth entry becomes `aspect_buildAndDeployment.txt`. The old code tried to read the hard-coded `aspect_build_and_deployment.txt`, which no longer existed, and the exception it threw skipped the `git-history.zip` step. That step now runs as well.

I left `LandscapeAnalyzer.java` alone. It also hard-codes `aspect_build_and_deployment.txt` (and the other four names) when reading these lists, so a renamed aspect will probably break it too. I didn't touch it because it's outside the export you described.
